purpose: Current-NIST reconciliation and routing of additional tungsten spectroscopy/information sources discovered during Glob 99073 follow-up.

source_ingestion_policy.rule: Every substantive unique publication, dataset, advisory, or information item discovered during the inquiry receives a Worldshepherd use or a negative-control role.
source_ingestion_policy.duplicates: Duplicate mirrors, navigation pages, and repeated copies of the same substantive source are provenance aliases, not independent evidence.
source_ingestion_policy.search_noise: Substantive off-topic publications surfaced by search may be routed as reusable methodology/domain intelligence or negative-control material; search appearance never grants Glob evidence weight.

sources.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database Holdings — Tungsten
sources.observed_access_state: W II: 2838 lines, all 2838 with level designations; 211 with transition probabilities.
sources.note: Current-authority scope control. Supersedes use of the 1964 line count for any claim about the present ASD holdings.

sources.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database Levels Data — W II
sources.observed_access_state: ASD reports 264 output entries; 263 are W II levels and the final entry is the W III ionization limit. Current evaluated level values include 10592.485, 50292.354, and 52087.110 cm^-1.
sources.note: Current-authority level graph for W II. Use for current Ritz relations and reconciliation against historical Laun values. Do not count the W III limit as a W II graph node.

current_asd.scope: Current NIST ASD holdings as accessed 2026-08-16.
current_asd.claims_boundary: Uniform endpoint probabilities are only a first approximation. Actual transition degrees are heterogeneous, and global motif selection/multiple testing must be modeled.

shared_level_relation.interpretation: The common-lower-level topology survives current NIST level evaluation. Numerical proximity remains a candidate feature only and requires current-ASD topology-preserving null testing and global multiple-testing correction.

corrections.superseded_statement: The 62-even/132-odd level counts describe the current W II graph.
corrections.replacement: Those counts describe Laun's 1964 194-level graph. The Kramida-Shirai/current W II graph has 76 even and 187 odd physical levels.

corrections.superseded_statement: NIST ASD's '264 levels found' means 264 physical W II graph nodes.
corrections.replacement: The output contains 263 physical W II levels plus a terminal W III ionization-limit row.

corrections.superseded_statement: The preliminary 1.61% same-even and 2.36% same-endpoint probabilities characterize current W II.
corrections.replacement: They characterize the historical 1964 graph only. The current uniform-endpoint approximation is about 1.316% same-even and 1.844% same-either-endpoint, before degree correction and global multiple-testing correction.

next_actions: Use NIST ASD ASCII output to acquire the current 2838-line W II transition table with level identities.
Extract the empirical transition degree distribution for the 76 even and 187 odd physical W II levels.
Compute exact current Ritz-vs-observed residuals for all generated target matches.
Run topology-preserving null tests on both historical-Laun and current-ASD graphs as separate datasets.
Apply family-wise or false-discovery-rate correction across all species, datasets, target states, tolerances, and motif searches.
